### Key Ways to Improve Your Prompt

1. **Separate "Ask/Design" from "Build & Deliver"**
   * **Problem:** You open with exploratory questions (*"how would it work? what programming languages... would we use?"*) and end with strict code-delivery rules (*"Whole project as one tar.gz... do not include any file that has not changed"*).
   * **Fix:** Drop the open-ended questions—you already decided on **Kotlin + Jetpack Compose**—and state requirements directly as build specs.

2. **Clarify the Repository Topology & Remove Leftover `.NET` Boilerplate**
   * **Problem:** You reference `terlingua.github.io`, then say the repo is `https://github.com/terlingua/terlingua-android/`, then include leftover notes about `"only a few files need to change"`, `"do not include any file that has not changed"`, and `"global.json ... dotnet 11 stable on fedora"`.
   * **Fix:** Explicitly tell the agent that `terlingua-android` is a **new, standalone Android repository** whose CI checks out `terlingua/terlingua.github.io` at build time to read/compile `content/books/` and `content/authors/`. Remove the `"changed files only"` and `global.json`/Fedora `.NET` instructions (unless you specifically want the CI to run `ObserverMagazine.ContentProcessor` from `terlingua.github.io`).

3. **Bound "Older Android" and "Latest Stable" Precisely**
   * **Problem:** `"older versions of Android"` could mean API 21 (Android 5) or API 28 (Android 9). Meanwhile, `"latest stable everything"` on Android currently means **AGP 9.1.x / Gradle 9.3+**, **Kotlin 2.4.x**, and **Android 16/17 (API 36/37)**. Notably, **AGP 9.x has built-in Kotlin support** and breaks if an LLM generates the legacy `org.jetbrains.kotlin.android` plugin.
   * **Fix:** Pin concrete bounds (e.g., `minSdk = 26` [Android 8.0] or `28` [Android 9], `compileSdk = 36`/`37`, `targetSdk = 36`), require a Gradle Version Catalog (`gradle/libs.versions.toml`), and tell the agent not to use deprecated AGP 8 patterns.

4. **Explicitly Ban Google Play Services**
   * **Problem:** If you ask for "local transfer", "QR scanning", or "modern Android", LLMs frequently pull in Google ML Kit or Nearby Connections—both of which depend on proprietary Google Play Services and fail on de-Googled / Obtainium-focused devices.
   * **Fix:** Explicitly state **zero Google Play Services dependencies** and **omit `android.permission.INTERNET` from `AndroidManifest.xml`** so the app is verifiably 100% offline.

5. **Fix the CI/Release Trap ("Every single push builds a FULL release APK")**
   * **Problem:** Two hidden bugs will break Obtainium if left unspecified:
     1. Triggering releases on *all* pushes publishes a GitHub Release on feature branches too; you want releases on pushes to **`main`** (and `workflow_dispatch`), while PRs only run build + tests.
     2. Android and Obtainium reject updates if `versionCode` doesn't **strictly increase** on every release.
   * **Fix:** Require a monotonic `versionCode` derived from CI (e.g., `github.run_number` + offset) and a clean tag/version scheme (e.g., `vYYYY.MM.DD-<run_number>`), plus a **single universal `.apk`** (not `.aab` or ABI splits) and a `.sha256` checksum asset.

6. **Define Exact Rules for Progress Sharing, Feedback, and Large Screens**
   * **Progress sharing:** Without merge rules, an import will overwrite local progress. Require **conflict-free merging** (keep `answeredCorrectly = local || incoming`, earliest `firstVisitedAt`, latest `updatedAt`) using the same JSON structure as `terlingua.github.io`'s `BookProgress` (`schemaVersion = 1`).
   * **Button feedback:** Specify *when* sound/haptics trigger and require a **Settings toggle** + respecting device silent/ringer mode so every tap doesn't annoyingly beep.
   * **Phones / Foldables / Tablets / Notebooks:** Name **Material 3 Adaptive (`ListDetailPaneScaffold` / `WindowSizeClass`)** plus keyboard/mouse/trackpad support (focus rings, Escape/arrow navigation, hover states) so notebook-style PCs actually feel native.

7. **Fix the Delivery Format**
   * **Problem:** Plain chat models can't hand you a binary `.tar.gz` cleanly, and `"no code comments"` can strip helpful notes on R8 rules or manifest intent-filters.
   * **Fix:** Ask for either direct workspace edits (if using an IDE/CLI coding agent) or a single reproducible script/full-file listing, and replace `"no code comments"` with `"no obvious/chatty comments; brief comments only for non-obvious platform quirks"`.

### Improved Prompt (Ready to Copy & Paste)

> **Goal**
> Build a complete, standalone, 100% offline native Android app repository for **`https://github.com/terlingua/terlingua-android/`** that packages the **Books** and **Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs)** from **`https://github.com/terlingua/terlingua.github.io`** (`content/books/` and `content/authors/`) into a fast, self-contained APK distributed via GitHub Releases and Obtainium (no Google Play).
>
> **Core Constraints**
> - **Language & UI:** 100% Kotlin + Jetpack Compose + Material 3 (plus themes matching `terlingua.github.io`: System, Light, Dark, Sepia, Solarized Light/Dark, High Contrast).
> - **Modern Stack & Latest Stable Dependencies:** Use Gradle Version Catalog (`gradle/libs.versions.toml`) with current stable releases (AGP 9.x with built-in Kotlin—do not apply legacy `org.jetbrains.kotlin.android`—Kotlin 2.4+, Compose BOM, Navigation 3 or type-safe Compose navigation, Room + SQLite FTS5, `kotlinx.serialization`, Coroutines/`Flow`).
> - **SDK Support:** `minSdk = 26` (Android 8.0) for broad older-device compatibility; `compileSdk = 36` (or `37`) and `targetSdk = 36`.
> - **Zero Proprietary Dependencies & Zero Network:** No Google Play Services, no Firebase, no analytics SDKs. Do **not** declare `android.permission.INTERNET` in `AndroidManifest.xml`. All book text, code highlighting, author info, and quizzes must be compiled into the APK at build time (ideally as a pre-populated SQLite DB with FTS5 full-text search in `assets/`).
> - **Content Pipeline:** Keep `content/books/` in `terlingua.github.io` unchanged. In GitHub Actions (and a local helper script), fetch `terlingua/terlingua.github.io` (sparse checkout of `content/books`, `content/authors`, and `tools/ObserverMagazine.ContentProcessor` if reusing it, or compile directly with a build tool) and bundle the compiled data into the Android build before assembling the APK.
>
> **Features Required**
> 1. **Library, Search & Reader:**
>    - Browse all books with chapter/section counts, reading time, tags, author card, and completion progress meter.
>    - Offline full-text search across books, chapters, and sections.
>    - Clean native rendering of Markdown prose, syntax-highlighted code blocks, blockquotes, and horizontally scrollable tables.
>    - Interactive single-answer (radio) and multiple-answer (checkbox) quizzes with immediate evaluation, retry, "show answer", explanations, and sticky `answeredCorrectly` progress matching `terlingua.github.io` (`BookProgress` schemaVersion `1`).
> 2. **Adaptive UX (Phones, Foldables, Tablets, Notebook-style Android PCs):**
>    - Use Material 3 Adaptive layouts (`WindowSizeClass` / `ListDetailPaneScaffold`) so tablets, unfolded foldables, and desktop/Chromebook windows show chapter TOC and content side-by-side.
>    - Full keyboard/mouse support (focus indicators, hover states, Esc/arrow navigation, smooth scrolling).
>    - Support Predictive Back and Edge-to-Edge across supported API levels.
> 3. **Button & Quiz Feedback (Visual + Audible + Tactile):**
>    - Centralize interactive button/answer feedback so presses provide Material 3 visual ripple/scale feedback, device-capable haptic feedback (`HapticFeedback` / `HapticFeedbackConstants`), and optional bundled lightweight audio cues (`SoundPool`).
>    - Add Settings toggles to independently enable/disable Sound and Haptics, and respect the device's silent/DND state for audio.
> 4. **Offline Progress Backup & Sharing (Zero Server):**
>    - Persist progress locally in Room/DataStore.
>    - Export/import a portable JSON file (`.terlingua-progress.json`, compatible with `BookProgress` `schemaVersion = 1`) via Android's Storage Access Framework (`CreateDocument` / `OpenDocument`) and Share Sheet (`FileProvider` + `ACTION_SEND` / `ACTION_VIEW` intent filters) so it works over messaging apps, email, Bluetooth, Syncthing, or local storage.
>    - Also support offline device-to-device transfer via QR code (single-book gzip+Base64 using open-source ZXing—no Play Services ML Kit) and/or local Wi-Fi/Hotspot (`NsdManager` + local socket).
>    - Imports must default to a **conflict-free merge** (OR `answeredCorrectly`, earliest `firstVisitedAt`, latest `updatedAt`) with a preview diff before applying, plus a Replace option.
>
> **CI/CD & Obtainium Distribution**
> - GitHub Actions workflow on `push` to `main` (plus `workflow_dispatch`):
>   - Fetch `terlingua/terlingua.github.io` content, compile book bundle, run unit + Compose UI tests, and build a **single universal signed release `.apk`** (not `.aab`, not ABI splits) with R8 minification enabled.
>   - Run PR checks (`pull_request` to `main`) that compile and test without publishing a release.
>   - Sign using these exact GitHub Secrets: `KEYSTORE_BASE64`, `KEYSTORE_PASSWORD`, `KEY_ALIAS`, `KEY_PASSWORD`.
>   - Generate a strictly monotonic `versionCode` (e.g., from `github.run_number`) and date/run-based `versionName`.
>   - Publish a **full GitHub Release** (never pre-release) on every push to `main`, attaching the signed `.apk` and a `.sha256` file, structured cleanly for Obtainium auto-updates.
>
> **Engineering & Output Expectations**
> - Follow clean architecture, SOLID principles, and unidirectional data flow (`ViewModel` + `StateFlow`).
> - Keep code concise; avoid obvious/noisy comments (only add brief comments for non-obvious Android API/R8 constraints).
> - Include complete `README.md` documentation covering local build steps, Obtainium setup (including how to record/pin the signing certificate SHA-256), and offline progress sharing.
> - Deliver the full repository files cleanly with exact file paths (or generate all files directly in the workspace, and tell me if anything needs manual setup).

### Quick Tip Before You Run It
If you are using an **autonomous coding agent** (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot Workspace, etc.) inside an empty `terlingua-android` folder, this prompt will let it scaffold, build, and test `./gradlew assembleDebug testDebugUnitTest` in one pass. If you are pasting into a **plain web chat**, ask it for *"Step 1: Project structure + Gradle/CI + Content compiler first, then Step 2: Android app code"* so it doesn't hit output token limits halfway through.

Goal
Build a complete, standalone, 100% offline native Android app repository for https://github.com/terlingua/terlingua-android/ that packages the Books and Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs) from https://github.com/terlingua/terlingua.github.io (content/books/ and content/authors/) into a fast, self-contained APK distributed via GitHub Releases and Obtainium (no Google Play).

Core Constraints

    Language & UI: 100% Kotlin + Jetpack Compose + Material 3 (plus themes matching terlingua.github.io: System, Light, Dark, Sepia, Solarized Light/Dark, High Contrast).

    Modern Stack & Latest Stable Dependencies: Use Gradle Version Catalog (gradle/libs.versions.toml) with current stable releases (AGP 9.x with built-in Kotlin—do not apply legacy org.jetbrains.kotlin.android—Kotlin 2.4+, Compose BOM, Navigation 3 or type-safe Compose navigation, Room + SQLite FTS5, kotlinx.serialization, Coroutines/Flow).

    SDK Support: minSdk = 26 (Android 8.0) for broad older-device compatibility; compileSdk = 36 (or 37) and targetSdk = 36.

    Zero Proprietary Dependencies & Zero Network: No Google Play Services, no Firebase, no analytics SDKs. Do not declare android.permission.INTERNET in AndroidManifest.xml. All book text, code highlighting, author info, and quizzes must be compiled into the APK at build time (ideally as a pre-populated SQLite DB with FTS5 full-text search in assets/).

    Content Pipeline: Keep content/books/ in terlingua.github.io unchanged. In GitHub Actions (and a local helper script), fetch terlingua/terlingua.github.io (sparse checkout of content/books, content/authors, and tools/ObserverMagazine.ContentProcessor if reusing it, or compile directly with a build tool) and bundle the compiled data into the Android build before assembling the APK.

Features Required

    Library, Search & Reader:

        Browse all books with chapter/section counts, reading time, tags, author card, and completion progress meter.

        Offline full-text search across books, chapters, and sections.

        Clean native rendering of Markdown prose, syntax-highlighted code blocks, blockquotes, and horizontally scrollable tables.

        Interactive single-answer (radio) and multiple-answer (checkbox) quizzes with immediate evaluation, retry, "show answer", explanations, and sticky answeredCorrectly progress matching terlingua.github.io (BookProgress schemaVersion 1).

    Adaptive UX (Phones, Foldables, Tablets, Notebook-style Android PCs):

        Use Material 3 Adaptive layouts (WindowSizeClass / ListDetailPaneScaffold) so tablets, unfolded foldables, and desktop/Chromebook windows show chapter TOC and content side-by-side.

        Full keyboard/mouse support (focus indicators, hover states, Esc/arrow navigation, smooth scrolling).

        Support Predictive Back and Edge-to-Edge across supported API levels.

    Button & Quiz Feedback (Visual + Audible + Tactile):

        Centralize interactive button/answer feedback so presses provide Material 3 visual ripple/scale feedback, device-capable haptic feedback (HapticFeedback / HapticFeedbackConstants), and optional bundled lightweight audio cues (SoundPool).

        Add Settings toggles to independently enable/disable Sound and Haptics, and respect the device's silent/DND state for audio.

    Offline Progress Backup & Sharing (Zero Server):

        Persist progress locally in Room/DataStore.

        Export/import a portable JSON file (.terlingua-progress.json, compatible with BookProgress schemaVersion = 1) via Android's Storage Access Framework (CreateDocument / OpenDocument) and Share Sheet (FileProvider + ACTION_SEND / ACTION_VIEW intent filters) so it works over messaging apps, email, Bluetooth, Syncthing, or local storage.

        Also support offline device-to-device transfer via QR code (single-book gzip+Base64 using open-source ZXing—no Play Services ML Kit) and/or local Wi-Fi/Hotspot (NsdManager + local socket).

        Imports must default to a conflict-free merge (OR answeredCorrectly, earliest firstVisitedAt, latest updatedAt) with a preview diff before applying, plus a Replace option.

CI/CD & Obtainium Distribution

    GitHub Actions workflow on push to main (plus workflow_dispatch):

        Fetch terlingua/terlingua.github.io content, compile book bundle, run unit + Compose UI tests, and build a single universal signed release .apk (not .aab, not ABI splits) with R8 minification enabled.

        Run PR checks (pull_request to main) that compile and test without publishing a release.

        Sign using these exact GitHub Secrets: KEYSTORE_BASE64, KEYSTORE_PASSWORD, KEY_ALIAS, KEY_PASSWORD.

        Generate a strictly monotonic versionCode (e.g., from github.run_number) and date/run-based versionName.

        Publish a full GitHub Release (never pre-release) on every push to main, attaching the signed .apk and a .sha256 file, structured cleanly for Obtainium auto-updates.

Engineering & Output Expectations

    Follow clean architecture, SOLID principles, and unidirectional data flow (ViewModel + StateFlow).

    Keep code concise; avoid obvious/noisy comments (only add brief comments for non-obvious Android API/R8 constraints).

    Include complete README.md documentation covering local build steps, Obtainium setup (including how to record/pin the signing certificate SHA-256), and offline progress sharing.

    Deliver the full repository files cleanly with exact file paths (or generate all files directly in the workspace, and tell me if anything needs manual setup).
